1: Plotting each pair as a point shows whether the two variables move together, so the pattern in the diagram is the evidence for any claim about them.
2: Correlation describes the direction and strength of a relationship. A strong correlation does not prove that one variable causes the other, because a third factor can drive both.
3: A line of best fit should follow the trend with roughly equal numbers of points on each side. It summarises the overall pattern and reduces the effect of any single point.
4: Reading across the line gives estimates inside the range of the data. Predictions far beyond the data are less reliable, because the trend may not continue.
